wiki-iran.standing: Wikipedia's Iran article, and how many people open it each day. A readership series like this one rises when a country stops being background and becomes the story, so it tracks public attention rather than events themselves.
wiki-iran.recent: Readership tracked a confrontation that crossed from threat into exchange: US strikes on Iran's southern provinces on 30 August, Iran's General Staff vowing 'crushing and devastating' retaliation, eight missiles intercepted over Jordan and a supertanker stopped after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent rose 3% to $90.97.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: The July peak of $105.30 has unwound to $88.24, but the direction turned again as the Iran confrontation moved from threat to exchange: Brent rose 3% to $90.97 on US strikes, and two tankers were attacked leaving the Strait of Hormuz. South Africa's petrol rises R1.34 a litre on Tuesday despite a stronger rand.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate, the light sweet crude that sets the US benchmark. It prices American refining margins and the pump, and it moves on supply — production quotas, sanctions, a strait — as much as demand.
wti.recent: The barrel has fallen through the 57-day window, from $96.83 on Jun 4 to $69.60 on Jul 6, before recovering to $83.90. The direction has since reversed: Brent rose 3% to $90.97 on renewed Middle East supply-disruption risk after strikes on Iran, and Washington's move into Venezuela's reserves adds 65 billion barrels to the supply picture.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a pipeline hub in Louisiana where major interstate lines meet. It prices the gas that heats American homes and fuels power plants, and it anchors the cost of LNG cargoes shipped abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The US benchmark has drifted down about 12% over the window to $2.70, hitting a low of $2.56 on Aug 7 — a domestic slide that has not followed through to the rest of the world. EU gas storage sits near 64% heading into winter, Delhi's compressed natural gas jumped ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg on surging LNG prices, and Pakistan apologized for night-time blackouts.

wheat.standing: The world benchmark price for a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. It moves on harvests, export bans and war in the growing regions, and bread, flour and food-aid budgets move after it.
wheat.recent: Wheat has climbed to $228.7 per tonne, the top of a run that began at $155.1 in September 2025. The coverage in this window does not name a supply event behind the rise, though it shows the downstream squeeze: the World Food Programme is halving its West Bank operation, cutting support for 400,000 people, and Pakistan's food imports rose 8.12pc to $805.5m in July.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple calorie for roughly half the planet and the grain most exposed to export bans, since only a small share of the crop is ever traded across borders.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen 16% over the series and sits at $464/mt, well below the $555.1 peak of Sep 2024 and above the Oct 2025 low of $330.6. The coverage does not identify what drove the move.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in almost everything that uses it. Wiring, motors, transformers and grid cable all run on it, so its price tracks how fast the world is building electrical capacity.
copper.recent: The series has climbed 46% from its December 2024 low of $8,910 to a June 2026 peak of $13,550, in a period defined by grid buildout: AI data-centre demand is reinventing the transformer, electric vehicles are straining grid voltage in London test networks, and the White House has banned foreign grid parts on security grounds. Mining pollution in Lualaba, DRC marks where the supply comes from.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the world's benchmark risk-free rate. It sets the floor under mortgages, corporate borrowing and sovereign debt pricing everywhere, and it rises when buyers demand more to hold Washington's paper.
us-10y.recent: The move came with pressure on central-bank independence: Warsh's Jackson Hole debut repriced the dollar, and Treasury Secretary Bessent urged Japan to raise rates, which would make Japanese buyers of US debt harder to find. Thirty-year yields reached 5.3% on 27 August, a 2007 level; the ten-year peaked at 4.75% on Jul 31.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, and the default measure of American equity performance. Most retirement money tracks it, so its level is what household wealth is quoted against.
sp500.recent: The index sits near the top of its 62-day range after an August dominated by the financing of the AI build-out: Nvidia pledged $500 billion to its own buyers, and BofA reiterated its Nvidia rating on that supply commitment strategy. Walmart shares were obliterated on 20 August, and the peak of 7,799 came on 13 August.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of large technology firms, so it is read as the market's price on the tech sector rather than the broad economy.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits below its Jun 15 high of 30540 after touching 27190 on Jul 29. Recent moves came from the sector's largest names: Apple named John Ternus CEO on Tuesday as Tim Cook stepped down to executive chairman, Nvidia paid $3.5 billion in bonds for a stake option in MediaTek, and Meta settled with 52 US states.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It follows crude, but with a lag and a floor: refining capacity, taxes and seasonal blending rules sit between the barrel and the gallon.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining, not crude, is where the pressure sits. Ukraine's drones struck the Samara oil refinery, Moscow's gas stations capped sales at 30 litres, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved" as Russia moved to import fuel and lower standards. US prices drifted down over the window, off the Jun 8 high of 4.146.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas at the Dutch TTF hub, the benchmark for gas traded across Europe. It sets what utilities, heavy industry and households ultimately pay for heat and power, and it moves on pipeline supply, storage levels and competition for seaborne LNG cargoes.
natgas-ttf.recent: The move follows a squeeze on European supply: EU storage sits near 64%, well below where it should be heading into winter, and Europe is bidding against Asian buyers for the same LNG cargoes. That competition has passed through beyond Europe, with Delhi raising compressed natural gas ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the US stock market over the coming month. It falls when markets are calm and spikes on shocks, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear rather than of value.
vix.recent: The index has drifted lower across the past three months, easing from 22.22 on Jun 10 to a low of 14.25 on Aug 14 and holding near that floor at 14.92. No single event accounts for the decline.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's exchange rate against the dollar, and the price at which Pakistan buys everything it imports. Fuel, wheat, medicine and machinery are invoiced in dollars, so a weaker rupee raises domestic prices and the cost of servicing external debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee drifted to 278.8 on Aug 31, its weakest of the month, against a run of import-side strain: Pakistan apologized for night-time blackouts after an RLNG cargo delay, and diesel carries an Rs114 levy after peaking at Rs520 a litre in April. Islamabad also sent its army chief to Istanbul for the first Mecca Pact committee meeting.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar. Nigeria imports most of its fuel and much of its food, so the naira's level sets domestic prices, and oil earnings in dollars are the state's main source of foreign exchange.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed to 1,333 from its 1,365 high on Aug 8 as Nigeria's foreign reserves hit a 20-year high, which Moody's rewarded with a better outlook on Abuja's austerity. FTSE Russell will also reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified to Frontier on September 21, a change that routes index money back to Lagos.

fx-egp.standing: The number of Egyptian pounds it takes to buy a US dollar. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel and services heavy external debt in dollars, so a weaker pound raises the price of bread, energy and repayment together.
fx-egp.recent: The pound drifted to 50.92 on Sep 2 from 49.56 on Aug 8, its weakest of the month, after the US cut off a major Egyptian bank from the global financial system on Aug 28. Xi Jinping arrived in Cairo the same week, with Egypt short of dollars and Suez transit revenue degraded by shipping disruption.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's price against the dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. Turkey imports most of its energy in dollars, so the rate feeds directly into domestic fuel and food prices.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low of 48.3 on Sep 2, down about 1.6 percent over the month from 47.55 on Aug 4, a steady slide rather than a single break. The month's Turkish news was diplomatic and military — the first Mecca defence pact committee in Istanbul, and Ankara summoning Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships — with nothing in it bearing on the currency.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka against the US dollar. It sets the import bill for a country that buys its fuel, wheat and cotton abroad and pays for them in dollars, while its garment exports and worker remittances are what earn those dollars back.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka held in a narrow band, near 123 to the dollar, ranging only between 124 on Aug 7 and 122 on Aug 19. Nothing in the month's news — the election of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as president, the confirmed purchase of Chinese J-10CE fighters — moved it beyond that range.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupiah. It is the price of Southeast Asia's largest economy, and it sets the cost of the fuel, food and dollar debt Indonesia imports.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah strengthened from 18,040 on Aug 4 to 17,650 by Aug 21 and has held near that level since. The month's Indonesian news was structural rather than monetary: Prabowo's tightening grip on the economy through cooperatives, the captive coal plants powering the Morowali nickel smelters, and RCEP's unclosed capital gap. None of it explains the move in the rate.

fx-lbp.standing: The street value of Lebanon's currency against the dollar, quoted per US dollar rather than the long-defunct official peg. It is the country's clearest gauge of confidence in the state: salaries, savings and import prices all move with it.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has been close to flat over the month, trading between 89,280 on Aug 8 and 89,980 on Aug 31, with no sign that the fighting in the south moved it. Lebanon's health ministry put the death toll from Israeli attacks at 4,350, and Israeli forces held Christian villages along the border, but the rate barely shifted.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the US dollar, managed within a band the People's Bank of China sets each morning rather than floated freely. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, and a weaker yuan makes everything China ships cheaper.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to its strongest level of the month, 6.721 on Sep 1, after China's factory gauge rose to 51.5 in August. The currency's use beyond trade settlement kept widening: Shanghai's crude benchmark gained measurable price independence, and China tripled the number of banks handling the digital yuan to 30. Washington spent the same week pressing G20 members to join its case against China's trade surplus.

fx-inr.standing: The price of one US dollar in Indian rupees, and the exchange rate that sets the cost of India's imported oil, fertiliser and electronics. A weaker rupee raises the bill for everything the country buys abroad and lifts what its exporters and its diaspora send home.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee firmed to its strongest level in a month after India's economy grew 7.8% in the June quarter, beating forecasts, and August vehicle sales pointed the same way, with Honda's two-wheelers up 8% at 579,000 units. The currency had been weakest on Aug 20, before either figure landed.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate between Brazil's currency and the US dollar, quoted as reais per dollar. Brazil is a major exporter of soy, iron ore, oil and beef, so the real moves with commodity demand, and its level sets the price of imported fuel and machinery.
fx-brl.recent: The real drifted weaker over the month, hitting 5.222 on Aug 15 after a low of 5.085 on Aug 10, and sits at 5.154. The collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe in Brasília put supervisory failure at the centre of the domestic financial story during the same stretch.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between Mexico's peso and the US dollar, and one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the peso absorbs shifts in US trade policy, rates and demand faster than almost any other.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso is a fraction stronger over the month, easing from 17.31 on Aug 4 to 16.92 by Aug 21 before settling near the middle of that range. Nothing in the month's news explains the drift: the trade-war headlines of late August concerned Canada, not Mexico.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro and the US dollar, the world's two largest reserve currencies. It sets the price of everything the euro area buys in dollars — energy, commodities, imported goods — and moves on the gap between European and American interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The euro slipped over the month, touching 0.8556 per dollar on Aug 20 before recovering to 0.8636. The month's European news ran to policy rather than money: Iceland voted 52.5% against reopening EU accession talks, Italy again extended Schengen border checks with Spain to September 15, and EU gas storage sat near 64% heading into winter.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker yen. It is the world's main funding currency for borrowing cheaply to invest elsewhere, and it sets the price Japan pays for imported food and fuel.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen fell past 160 per dollar on 31 August, putting traders on intervention watch, with the rate gap widening as thirty-year Treasury yields reached 5.3%, a 2007 level. US Treasury Secretary Bessent then publicly urged Japan to raise rates, pressing a nominally independent Bank of Japan.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. It carries the price of Russian oil earnings, the cost of imports, and the pressure of sanctions into domestic prices.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened through a week in which Russians moved 4.2 trillion rubles into cash, Zelenskyy named Moscow and St. Petersburg as drone targets, and US Treasury signalled a further bank designation without naming it. Oil leverage held: India remains Russia's second-largest crude buyer, and Siluanov returned to the G20 despite a European boycott.

fx-zar.standing: The rand against the dollar, the most traded currency of any emerging African economy and a standing proxy for global risk appetite. It is priced off mining exports, and it sets the local cost of imported fuel, machinery and debt.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through late August, from 16.52 on Aug 4 to a low of 15.92 on Aug 26, but the stronger currency did not reach the pump: petrol rises R1.34 a litre on Tuesday, as South Africa's fuel formula passes through a war premium the exchange rate cannot offset.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the oldest and largest cryptocurrency, quoted against the dollar. It trades continuously and is held by funds, corporate treasuries and individuals, which makes it a live gauge of appetite for risk outside the banking system.
btc.recent: The run from $62,840 on Aug 17 to $80,020 was a short squeeze rather than a leveraged rally, as open interest collapsed while the price rose. Traders positioned for Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, and BlackRock cut its in-kind swap threshold from $25 million to $1 million. Strategy then spent $635 million defending its own stock.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum network, used to pay for transactions and contracts on it. It is the second-largest cryptocurrency by value, and the settlement asset beneath most tokenised finance, so what happens on the chain shows up in its price.
eth.recent: The rise came in a broad crypto rally on 20 August, when bitcoin broke a six-week range above $71,000 and roughly $3 billion in bearish bets were wiped out; one trader lost $24 million on ether in twelve seconds. Treasury buybacks and a weaker dollar lifted risk appetite, while Washington's securities regulator proposed a crypto rulebook on 23 August.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated gold bullion, so its price tracks a troy ounce of the metal. Gold is the asset people move into when they doubt currencies or central banks, and it pays nothing to hold.
paxg.recent: The move ran through Jackson Hole: bitcoin and gold were pricing Warsh's Friday speech and the question of Fed independence, and the peak came on Aug 25 before the series eased back to $4,315. Physical demand showed the same pull — in Kassala, street dealers now outbid the licensed market.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A daily count of how many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence — a rough gauge of general public curiosity about the field, rising when the technology reaches audiences beyond the industry that builds it.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership tracked a run of regulatory and legal decisions rather than any product launch: the EU placed ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox under its 'very large platform' rules, and a US court ruled the Pentagon ban of Anthropic unlawful, with a judge calling it "illegal and baseless." Bill Gates also drew wide pickup warning of a 'turbulent' AI transition.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia — the world's largest country by land area, a nuclear-armed permanent member of the UN Security Council, and one of the biggest exporters of oil, gas and grain.
wiki-russia.recent: Readership tracked a war that widened past Ukraine: the 17 August peak came amid Russian missile strikes on Kyiv that killed at least 13 as air defences faltered, and attention held through a strike on an arms depot near Bucha whose stored shells detonated and killed 37, Niger's army asking Moscow to crush a mutiny, and Siluanov's return to the G20 table over European objection.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of some 250 million people. Attention here tracks whichever story pulls outside readers in — a court fight, a flood, a defence pact — rather than anything about the country itself.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The 14 August peak sat alongside Pakistan's independence anniversary and a run of political news: Imran Khan was moved back to jail after a medical checkup on 21 August, and Asim Munir visited Tehran on 24 August to revive Pakistan's Iran mediation. A hospital nursery fire in the capital killed 14 newborns on 26 August, and the first committee meeting under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement opened in Istanbul on 31 August.

wiki-china.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on China. It is a rough gauge of where general attention lands, rising when a country moves from background to foreground for readers with no particular stake in it.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak sits before the current run of stories; the rise since has tracked events on China's borders and balance sheet. A glacial flood on the Nepal-China border has killed more than 1,000 across Nepal and Tibet, Vietnam has demanded China halt construction on two Paracel features, and Xi Jinping arrived in Cairo after a decade away.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that connects the Gulf to open ocean, and the narrowest point in the global oil trade. A fifth of the world's oil transits it, so any interruption there is priced into fuel and freight everywhere else.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership tracked the closure fight: Iran said transit required Tehran's permission, the IRGC claimed a veto, and 6,000 sailors were left stranded aboard anchored ships. US strikes on Larak Island and attacks on two tankers leaving Hormuz followed, pushing Brent 3% higher to $90.97.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up on any given day.
wiki-india.recent: Readership rose through a week of Indian diplomacy at the SCO summit in Bishkek, where Modi met Putin and Xi, held talks with Iran's President Pezeshkian, and pressed for peace in Ukraine while India kept buying Russian crude as Moscow's second-largest oil customer. India also grew 7.8% in the June quarter and agreed with Uzbekistan to seek $5 billion in trade by 2030.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country itself rather than a single event, and one that rises when the war forces a general audience to check the basics.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak came as Ukraine's allies convened in Kyiv and Zelensky pressed for an air defence boost; a second wave followed the 29 August strike on an arms depot near Kyiv, where stored shells rather than the strike itself killed 37, and the Zaporizhzhia plant lost off-site power, running a week on diesel alone.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed as Iran declared that Hormuz transit now requires Tehran's permission and two tankers were attacked leaving the strait. A supertanker was stopped after hitting mines, US strikes hit Larak Island, and 6,000 sailors remain stuck aboard anchored ships. Brent rose 3% to $90.97, and Delhi's CNG jumped ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits well below its own baseline as the Houthis keep striking shipping: a missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, and Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Razih district the same day. Owners are still routing around a corridor where crews are being injured rather than through it.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic is running near its 90-day baseline but well below the 57 vessels/day peak of 11 August, with Red Sea risk still keeping owners away: Houthis said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia on 24 August, and Pakistani nationals injured in an earlier Houthi attack in the Red Sea returned home. Cairo's transit revenue is one of the shortages shaping Xi Jinping's visit.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has drifted down through the window, from 264 vessels a day on Jun 22 to 192, running about 8.5% below its own 90-day baseline with calm seas and no weather alert. The coverage does not explain the decline.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic is down about 18 percent across the window and sits 2.6 percent below its own 90-day baseline, with a swing from 28 vessels on 10 July to 401 two days later. Nothing in the record explains the July swing; the strait's political backdrop has stayed noisy, with Vietnam demanding China halt construction on two Paracel features and Washington rallying G20 partners against China's surplus.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits are running 13% below their 90-day baseline, at 28 vessels a day against a July 13 high of 83, after the Panama Canal moved to cap daily transits anticipating a severe El Niño. Separately, Hong Kong's CK Hutchison is seeking HK$11.7b from Panama in a dispute over the canal's ports.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has fallen through the summer, and Turkey now says its own ships are being hit: Ankara summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish vessels in the Black Sea, the trade the strait carries. Daily transits are running about a sixth below their 90-day baseline.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic is running about 5.8% below its 90-day baseline, with 119 vessels a day against a 163-vessel peak on Jun 13. The coverage does not explain the decline: the Italy-Spain Schengen suspension renewed to September 15 checks land borders, not shipping, and the Hormuz closure sits at the other end of the route.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has drifted down over the window, running about 6% below its 90-day baseline, with a high of 186 vessels on Aug 1 and a low of 126 two days later on Aug 3. Nothing in the record explains the swing; seas were calm, with waves peaking at 1.3 metres.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic swung between 68 vessels on Jul 27 and 123 on Jul 31, and the last week sits level with its 90-day baseline. A Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on Aug 24, the kind of strike that pushes owners onto this route rather than the Red Sea. Rough seas, with waves to 3.3m, hold on the cape itself.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has stopped: the strait has recorded no vessels since 17 July, running 97 percent below its own 90-day baseline with calm seas and no weather alert. The Black Sea around it is now a shooting range — Turkey summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships, and Moscow is pitching an Arctic route as the safer corridor.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits near the bottom of a 35-day slide, down roughly 3% from its Jun 16 high of 11,150 to a Jul 15 low of 10,700. Riyadh spent August signing a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey, shelling villages in Yemen's Razih district, and awaiting US congressional review of a nuclear deal tied to recognition of Israel.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its two-month range after a run of diplomatic activity in Istanbul: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey held the first committee meeting under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement on 31 August, with Pakistan sending its army chief. Turkey also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships in the Black Sea.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its range after the UAE downed an Iranian drone over its territorial waters on 31 August, and Washington moved against Emirati banks over Iran ties. Hormuz disruption is already in the real economy: hotel demand fell to 7% of normal levels and Gulf solar-panel imports dropped up to 90%.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index slipped from its Aug 26 high of 1749 after prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri with concealing some $40 million in assets on Aug 27, reviving the political-risk discount Malaysian equities carried through the last asset-concealment case. It still sits above its Jul 1 low of 1657.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth since its June low, closing at a high on Sep 1 as Prabowo tightened the state's grip on the economy through cooperatives and the nickel boom in Morowali ran on captive coal power. Gains held despite unresolved questions over gig-driver classification and RCEP's persistent capital gap.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index fell as the yen slid past 160 per dollar and US Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly urged the Bank of Japan to raise rates — pressure on a nominally independent central bank that forces traders to price a political input into the rate path. Tighter policy would lift the yen and squeeze exporter earnings.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index has drifted lower across the window despite a firmer mainland economy, with China's factory gauge rising to 51.5 in August. Hong Kong took Shein's listing at a discounted $26.3bn valuation, a venue of last resort for a company shut out elsewhere, while Washington used the G20 to rally other governments behind tariffs against China's surplus.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index has drifted down about 3% over the window despite China's factory gauge rising to 51.5 in August, a reading the PMI story shows was carried by AI-linked capital spending rather than broad demand. Trade politics stayed unhelpful: at the G20 the US Treasury pressed other nations to join its case against China's surplus.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen roughly a quarter over the window, with the Bank of Korea hiking rates to 3.00% on 27 August tightening conditions further. Washington's cancellation of next month's Twin Dragons exercise and Trump's announced meeting with Kim Jong Un reset the security backdrop; SK Hynix is weighing closer ties with Kioxia.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 66-day range after India's economy grew 7.8% in the June quarter and Honda's two-wheelers sold 579,000 units in August, up 8%. The latest session gave some of that back as Sun Pharma tied US Medicaid prices to its global floor, a commitment made by one of the market's largest drugmakers.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed steadily since June, reaching 5,768 on Aug 17 before easing. Singapore's role as a trade and finance conduit ran through the period: a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties, and crypto card spending in the city tripled to $1.04 billion.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Nvidia paid $3.5 billion in bonds for a stake option in MediaTek, sending MediaTek shares up 10% and cementing it as an AI player. The index still slipped 1.6% on the day, and remains below its Jun 22 high of 47,740 after bottoming at 39,930 on Jul 30. Taiwan also indicted nine people, including an Nvidia manager, over AI server smuggling.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index fell 3.8% in a day to 1,577, leaving it slightly below where it stood a month ago after a 1,639 high on Jul 17 and a 1,541 low on Jun 23. Nothing in the available material accounts for the drop.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits at 6,046 after a 5.6% single-day fall, giving back most of a run that peaked at 6,404 on Jul 17 and leaving it only modestly above its Jun 8 low of 5,879. Nothing in the available reporting from Manila accounts for the drop.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index fell about 1.2% on 1 September, sliding on a Trump vow, as Australian home prices fell for a fifth straight month and homebuyer numbers collapsed. That downturn arrives with rate cuts constrained by imported energy inflation, and the corporate mood matched it: KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff, about 5% of its workforce.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index has climbed roughly 3% over the window, reaching 118,200 on Aug 28 before easing to 115,900. The coverage in this period is domestic policy rather than market news — a R1.34 a litre petrol increase on Tuesday that held despite a stronger rand, and R88.6bn in unclaimed dormant accounts and pensions eyed by Treasury — and does not explain the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index climbed to 179,700 on Sep 1, its high over the window and 4.37% above where it started, recovering from the Aug 18 low of 166,300. The main domestic financial event in that stretch was the collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe in Brasília, a supervisory failure rather than a market-wide shock.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down about 4% over the past 65 days, from its Jun 2 high of 68,890 to a Aug 18 low of 63,930, and closed at 65,430. The input names no Mexican policy or market event behind the slide.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits near the lower end of a 64-day range that peaked on Jul 22 and bottomed on Aug 19, down about 6 percent across the window. The input names no Argentine market event behind the move.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index has slid from its Aug 25 high of 36,960 as the trade fight escalated: Canada vowed a 'dollar-for-dollar' response to US tariffs and refused relief on heavy trucks, Ontario Premier Doug Ford backed retaliation including a threatened power cutoff, and Trump demanded Canadian companies relocate to the US.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index slipped as the US–Iran exchange widened: US strikes on Iran, an Iranian drone downed offshore by the United Arab Emirates, and a supertanker stopped after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Daniel Driscoll resigned as Army secretary amid Pentagon unease over the Iran war.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a broad climb from the June low, but the London news of the past week points elsewhere than equities: Brent crude rose 3% to $90.97 on the Iran strikes, and the London Stock Exchange set out plans for tokenized UK shares.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached its high on Aug 28 before slipping, with security incidents accumulating around German infrastructure: explosive devices were found near a power plant on Sep 1, and Berlin prepared Russia sanctions after a bomb-rigged drone landed near a cargo plane at Leipzig. EU gas storage sits at a record low.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Paris-listed defence and space names have had a run of contract news: Sweden signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates from Naval Group, and the European Space Agency awarded €544 million to three rocket startups. The index sits below its Aug 10 high of 8726 but well above the Jun 1 low of 8147.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up around 6% over the past two months and off its Aug 13 high of 1120, with a small daily decline. Nothing in the window explains the move: the only market news at hand is the EU entering what the Guardian called 'winter panic' mode as gas storage hit a record low on Aug 29.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed roughly a tenth over the past three months, from a low of 18,140 on Jun 10 to a peak of 20,210 on Aug 11, and sits near that high. Nothing in the recent Spanish news — Italy's renewed 15-day suspension of Schengen border checks with Spain, or the Bronze Age museum theft — accounts for the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a summer climb, with the high of 53,720 on Aug 7 giving way to a 1.3% drop on the latest session. Nothing in the Italian news of the past fortnight explains that fall — Rome's extension of Schengen border checks with Spain to September 15 is a movement question, not a market one.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, up about 8 percent since early June, with the high on Aug 10 and the low on Jun 3. Nothing in the available material accounts for the move.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index touched its 66-day high of 3331 on Aug 28, days before Stockholm signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates from Naval Group at €1.1 billion each — an order placed abroad rather than with a domestic yard. It has since slipped 1.3% to 3266.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index sits at 4,057, down about 4% across the past 64 days from its 12 June high of 4,292 and near the 29 June low of 3,966. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the coming meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with anything that changes the case for a cut or a hike — inflation prints, jobs data, and what Fed officials say in public.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and the market for no change ran up to 75 on 15 August before falling back to 41. Warsh's Jackson Hole speech on 28 August, that the Fed will have "work to do" if inflation doesn't fade, pushed the same way; traders bet on Fed hikes as Bitcoin fell under $79,000.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia biography of the sitting US president, and one of the most-read pages on the site. Daily readership rises whenever he acts — a policy, a post, a court ruling — making it a rough gauge of how far his decisions are travelling.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The 26 August peak came amid the Iran escalation: Trump posted about Iran 319 times as his war aims shifted, then posted a fake video of the Kharg Island oil terminal exploding, and declared Hormuz clear when the strait was not reopened. Readership has since fallen back to about half that level.

wiki-stablecoin.standing: A crypto token designed to hold a fixed value, usually one US dollar, by holding reserves against every coin issued. It is the settlement layer for most crypto trading, and increasingly a way to move dollars across borders outside correspondent banking.
wiki-stablecoin.recent: Attention tracked banks moving onto the rails rather than around them: 21 major institutions, Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs and UBS among them, are forming a single company to issue a stablecoin compliant with the US GENIUS Act and the EU's MiCA. The late-August climb followed Standard Chartered distributing Hong Kong's dollar stablecoin, Shinhan building won rails with a card network, and crypto card spending tripling to $1.04 billion.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on the United States — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up, rising when Washington is at the centre of an international story.
wiki-united-states.recent: The 28 August peak sat between two US-Iran exchanges: American jets struck Larak Island on 30 August, hitting two Iranian launchers, and Tehran vowed crushing revenge after strikes on its southern coast. The UAE downed an Iranian drone offshore, and a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The number of people reading Wikipedia's Bitcoin article each day — a rough gauge of how far the asset has pushed past its own audience into general curiosity, which tends to track price moves rather than lead them.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Readership rose with the price: Bitcoin surged to $80,020, up 23.7% in a week, on what turned out to be a short squeeze rather than a leveraged rally, and the peak on Aug 24 followed a shariah board in Ras Al Khaimah clearing Bitcoin trading at Rakbank Islamic. BlackRock then cut its swap-in threshold from $25 million to $1 million.

wiki-nepal.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Nepal, the Himalayan state between India and China. Attention to a country page tends to be flat for months and then jump when something happens there that the rest of the world has reason to look up.
wiki-nepal.recent: A glacial lake outburst flood tore down a valley on the Nepal-China border on 26 August, and the peak on Aug 27 tracked the first full day of counting: deaths passed 1,000 across Nepal and Tibet, with 934 workers trapped or missing at hydropower sites and 320 Indians uncontactable. India sent a tunnel rescue team and 37.5 tonnes of aid.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve targets for overnight lending between banks. It is the price of dollars at the shortest maturity, and mortgages, corporate borrowing and the value of the dollar are all repriced from it.
fed-funds.recent: The target has sat at 3.75% since December 2025, a quarter below its September 2024 peak of 5%, and the direction of the next move has flipped. Fed minutes from 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and markets now favor a September hike after Warsh's Jackson Hole debut.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks to park cash with it overnight. It is the floor under euro borrowing costs, so mortgages, business loans and the euro's exchange rate all take their cue from it.
ecb-rate.recent: The rate sits at 2.25%, down from 3.5% in Sep 2024 and a notch above the 2% low of Jun 2025, as easing gave way to a global turn back toward tightening. Markets now favor a September rate hike from the Fed, and the Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00%.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans who want work and cannot find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when it sets interest rates, and the one voters feel first.
us-unemployment.recent: The rate stands at 4.1%, unchanged over the window and near the bottom of its recent range — down from the 4.5% high of November 2025, and just above the 4.0% low of January 2025. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest economy. The count rises when the country enters a news cycle, so it works as a rough gauge of outside attention.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Attention drifted down through August as Nigeria's news turned domestic and technical. Foreign reserves hit a 20-year high and FTSE Russell moved to reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified on September 21; petrol imports reached 43% of supply in July, and Atiku vowed to restore petrol subsidy if elected in 2027.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a parliamentary majority since the 2000s, wins the most seats in Russia's State Duma election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The contract climbed from 64 on Aug 3 to a high of 75 on Aug 30 and sits at 71, firming through a month in which Russia's diplomatic position hardened rather than weakened: Modi called for dialogue over battlefield solutions at the SCO summit in Bishkek, Trump welcomed Russia at the G20 over EU objections, and four EU states reopened the frozen-assets debate.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States lifts its naval blockade of Iranian shipping by a set date. Traders buy and sell a yes-or-no outcome, and the price is what they are willing to pay for it — a running read on how a war's end is being wagered.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The price collapsed from 24% on Aug 27 to 6% as the confrontation widened rather than wound down: US strikes on Larak Island, Iran's vow of crushing revenge after jets hit its southern coast, eight missiles downed over Jordan and an Iranian drone downed by the United Arab Emirates. Iran also set terms requiring Tehran's permission for Hormuz transit.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether U.S. forces mount a ground invasion of Iran within the period. It is a price traders pay for that outcome, so it tracks how a confrontation is being read as it escalates — not a forecast, but what money is being staked.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The odds fell even as the fighting widened: US strikes hit Larak Island on Sunday and Iran's southern coast, Iran vowed crushing revenge, Jordan downed eight missiles and the UAE shot down an Iranian drone. Traders read air strikes, sanctions and Iran's Hormuz permission regime as an air-and-economic campaign rather than a prelude to invasion.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A traded contract on whether Israel and Iran will hold a ceasefire by a set date. The price is what buyers will pay for that outcome, so it moves with the fighting itself — and with the shipping, insurance and oil markets that price the same war.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The odds slid from 89 on Aug 25 to 78 as the confrontation moved from threat to exchange: US strikes on Larak Island on Aug 30, Iran's vow of revenge for strikes on its southern coast, eight missiles downed over Jordan and an Iranian drone downed by the United Arab Emirates. Brent rose 3% to $90.97 as Tehran set terms for Hormuz transit.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each shift in the campaign rather than with any single poll.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The contract climbed from 25% on Aug 3 to a high of 41% on Aug 31, a rise of more than half over the month. Nothing in the available material identifies what drove it.

xag.standing: A token backed by an ounce of vaulted physical silver, so its price tracks the metal. Silver is both a monetary hedge and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics, brazing — so investor and factory demand both move it.
xag.recent: The series ran from $29.81 on Aug 6 to a peak of $69.42 on Aug 28 and has since eased to $63.91. Nothing available here accounts for the move.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The daily count of people opening Wikipedia's article on petroleum — the fossil liquid refined into fuels, plastics and fertiliser. Readership climbs when supply is threatened or ownership changes hands, so it tracks who is suddenly thinking about oil.
wiki-petroleum.recent: The peak on Aug 13 sat between two stories that changed who owns and who ships crude: Washington's move on Venezuela's reserves, where 65 billion barrels changed hands and the Pentagon took a stake through North American Blue Energy Partners, and the widening pressure on Iran that pushed Brent up 3% to $90.97 before two tankers were attacked leaving Hormuz.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro, a Brazilian senator and son of the former president, places second in a presidential election. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is a market's cash view of a family's grip on the right.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.recent: The contract has traded in a narrow band, between 81 on Aug 3 and 88 on Aug 6, with nothing in the window explaining the drift to 86.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether J.D. Vance becomes the Republican presidential nominee in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as party standing, rivals and scandal shift.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.recent: The contract climbed from 43 on Aug 8 to 53, its high on Sep 2, over a month in which prediction markets themselves were the story rather than the field. A White House aide who read speeches early was fined for betting on them, and the Ninth Circuit ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts aren't "swaps," confirming state powers over the venues.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic nominee for the 2028 presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on party manoeuvring rather than on any vote yet cast.
poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.recent: The odds drifted down across the month, from 9% on Aug 3 to a low of 7% on Aug 13, with nothing in the nomination race behind it. What moved around prediction markets was regulation and scandal: the Ninth Circuit ruled Kalshi's sports bets aren't "swaps", Connecticut sued, and a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine over bets on the president's speeches.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A prediction market on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will hold Israel's premiership after the next change of government. It prices political survival for a leader whose coalition arithmetic, corruption trial and war decisions are all bound together.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: The contract fell through August as Israel's campaign widened rather than closed: strikes in Gaza, an airstrike on a home under construction in Jenin, a drone strike in Beit Jinn in southern Syria, and Israeli forces holding Lebanese Christian villages at Ain Ebel and Rmeish. Turkey moved to seek an Interpol notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla case.

poly-iran-full-airspace-closure-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran closes its airspace entirely before a set date. It is a bet, not a forecast: the price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves when the odds of a wider air war do.
poly-iran-full-airspace-closure-by-septe.recent: The odds have fallen by roughly two-thirds from their 36% peak on Aug 3 even as the fighting widened, because the exchanges have stayed maritime rather than aerial: Iran set terms requiring its permission for Hormuz transit, the IRGC claimed a veto over the strait, and a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines there. Airspace itself stayed open through the Larak strikes and the Jordan intercepts.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve holds its policy rate flat through the whole of 2026. It is a bet on the central bank staying put, so it prices how firmly traders think inflation has stopped falling.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: The contract has sat near the top of its range all month, and the Fed's own minutes released on 19 August, which showed many officials saying rate hikes may be needed, left little room for it to fall. Traders moved the other way too, betting on Fed hikes as Bitcoin slipped under $79,000 on 27 August.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces exchange fire directly by a set date. It prices how close traders think the war in Ukraine is to pulling the alliance in, rather than staying a war fought between Russia and Ukraine alone.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: Traders bid the contract up to 21% on Aug 27, the week Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead and four EU states moved to unlock Russia's frozen billions. It has fallen back to 12% since, with Modi calling for dialogue over battlefield solutions at the Shanghai bloc's Bishkek summit.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if crude oil sets a new all-time high before a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with anything that could squeeze supply — war, sanctions, an OPEC decision.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: The contract has drifted down over the month, from 14% on Aug 19 to 12%, with a low of 10% on Aug 9. Nothing in the oil market explains the move; the prediction-market news of the period was regulatory and legal, including a Ninth Circuit ruling on state powers over Kalshi and a fine against a White House aide who bet on the president's speeches.

stocks:META.standing: Meta Platforms runs Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, and sells the advertising that reaches their users. Its share price is a bet on attention: how many hours people spend in those feeds, and what an advertiser will pay to interrupt them.
stocks:META.recent: The stock fell after 52 US states settled with Meta for $17.1bn over social media harms to children, a sum worth roughly 1% of the company's stock value. The settlement's real cost is the product changes it buys — teen-safety defaults Meta will ship globally, having lobbied for softer rules where enforcement is thin.

poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marine Le Pen wins the 2027 French presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with the campaign, the field of rivals, and the legal constraints on who can run.
poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.recent: The 32-day rise to a high of 34 on Aug 28 came without a French political event in this window; the news around Polymarket concerned the platform itself rather than the race. One Polymarket study found 152 wallets with a 97.2% win rate, and a Ninth Circuit ruling on Aug 28 curbed rival Kalshi by holding that sports bets aren't "swaps.

poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Anthropic will hold the top-rated AI model when the period closes. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves as rivals ship new models and as benchmark rankings change.
poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.recent: The contract sat at 78% on Aug 11 and reached 94% on Aug 31, its high for the window, closing at 91%. Nothing in the record explains the move. Polymarket itself was in the news over the period: a report on 152 wallets showing a 97.2% win rate, and a White House aide fined over bets on the president's speeches.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the gateway between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, closes to shipping by a set date. Traders price the risk that a chokepoint carrying a large share of Europe–Asia trade shuts.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The contract has drifted down from 14% on Aug 19 to 5% on Aug 30, and the input carries no news about the strait itself to explain the fall. The Polymarket news in this window concerns the market venue rather than the waterway: reporting on 152 Polymarket wallets with a 97.2% win rate, and a Ninth Circuit ruling on state powers over prediction markets.

stocks:1919.HK.standing: China's largest container shipping line, and one of the biggest in the world by fleet capacity. Its share price tracks freight rates, which rise when trade routes are disrupted and fall when there is too much capacity chasing too little cargo.
stocks:1919.HK.recent: The stock has climbed over the past month, reaching 17.95 HKD on Aug 21 before easing to 16.61. Allegations that COSCO's cargo ships gather intelligence on trade routes place the fleet at the centre of a question about who controls the world's shipping lanes.

stocks:SUNPHARMA.NS.standing: India's largest drugmaker by revenue, and one of the biggest suppliers of generic medicines to the United States. Its earnings turn on US generic pricing and on regulatory clearance of its Indian plants.
stocks:SUNPHARMA.NS.recent: Sun Pharma tied its US Medicaid prices to its floor, accepting a most-favoured-nation clause that removes the differential pricing the industry has long defended. The stock is down about 1.4% over the past three weeks, easing from a high of 1,985 on Aug 31.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Gavin Newsom becomes the Democratic Party's nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with the field of rivals, not with any single poll.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.recent: The slide came alongside a bad month for the venues themselves rather than anything about Newsom: the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports bets are not "swaps" and confirmed state powers over prediction markets, Connecticut filed a fresh suit against Kalshi, and a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine over trading on speeches he read early.

poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez becomes the Democratic nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on primary field news rather than on polling alone.
poly-will-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-win-t.recent: The series ran from 9% on Aug 4 to a high of 14% on Aug 24 before easing to 11%, and the input names nothing about the 2028 Democratic field that accounts for the move. The month's Polymarket news concerned the platform itself rather than this contract.

poly-will-gabriel-attal-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Gabriel Attal, the former French prime minister and Renaissance party leader, becomes president. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as candidates enter, exit and are tested by scandal.
poly-will-gabriel-attal-win-the-2027-fre.recent: Nothing in the French race explains the drift from 5% on Aug 24 to 3%; the market has traded in a narrow band all month. The prediction-market news of the period was elsewhere: a Ninth Circuit ruling that sports bets aren't "swaps," and a White House aide fined for betting on speeches he read early.

xmr.standing: A privacy-focused cryptocurrency whose ledger hides sender, receiver and amount by default. That opacity makes it the settlement asset of choice for ransomware payments and sanctions-evading trade, and a recurring target of exchange delistings.
xmr.recent: The rise coincided with a stretch of reporting on payment channels that avoid the banking system: CISA identified more than 200 victims of Medusa ransomware over the past year, and North Korea's sanctions evasion toolkit drew fresh scrutiny as Pyongyang earns revenue without touching banks. The series peaked at $520.6 on Sep 1.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether JD Vance wins the 2028 US presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on primary results, endorsements and anything that changes who is running.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.recent: The contract drifted from 20% on Aug 21 to 25% on Aug 30, with no candidate news behind it. What moved around Polymarket instead was scrutiny of the venue: a White House aide who read Trump's speeches early paid a fine to settle an insider-trading case on Aug 29, and the Ninth Circuit ruled sports bets are not "swaps.

poly-will-magdalena-andersson-be-the-nex.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Magdalena Andersson becomes Sweden's next prime minister. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with the Social Democrats' standing and with the arithmetic of who can assemble a majority in the Riksdag.
poly-will-magdalena-andersson-be-the-nex.recent: Traders have held the contract high all month, but it has drifted down from 93 on Aug 24 to 79 on Sep 2. Nothing in the available reporting explains the slide.

stocks:V.standing: The card network that moves money between banks when a shopper taps or types a card number. It earns a fee on the flow rather than lending, so its revenue tracks consumer spending and cross-border travel worldwide.
stocks:V.recent: The stock traded between $358.8 on Aug 17 and $384.1 on Aug 25, ending the window at $372.7. Shinhan Financial tapped Visa on Aug 26 to build AI and stablecoin payments — a bank building rails with a card network, not around one — while VTB switched on QR payments in two more countries, outside the card networks entirely.

stocks:MA.standing: The card network behind Mastercard-branded credit and debit payments, earning a fee on transactions it routes between banks and merchants rather than lending itself. Its volumes track consumer spending across most of the world.
stocks:MA.recent: The card networks are extending their rails rather than defending them: Coinbase, Cloudflare and Mastercard are building wallets so AI agents can pay, and in Seoul, Shinhan is building won stablecoin rails with a card network rather than around one. The competing move is VTB's, which switched on QR payments in two more countries outside the card networks entirely.
